title: A Project Is a Boundary, Not a Big Idea
excerpt: Landscape photographer Ian Worth found his shooting had settled into a loop: scout, wait for light, take the frame, repeat. His answer is a long-term project with a boundary around it, and the boundary is what makes it work.

title: A Good Camera Was Never Just About Image Quality
excerpt: Premium phones are booming and cheap point-and-shoot cameras are booming at the same time. The contradiction says something useful about what photographers actually want from a camera.

title: The Most Important Gear Gets You to the Shot
excerpt: A travel photographer who shoots with a Sony a7CR and a Fujifilm X-H2 names a headlamp, not a lens, as the piece of gear he will not leave home without. The reason says a lot about how good photographs actually happen.
